candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (JERRS)
candidates.why_relevant: The single canonical application enumerating every licensed/registered financial market entity in CZ: banks, payment institutions (platební instituce), e-money institutions, small-scale payment service providers (PPSMR), small-scale e-money issuers, plus PSD2 notifications from foreign TPPs. This is the definitive competitor/actor universe for CZ payments — including fintechs that never appear in media — and each entry is a launch point for vendor, partner and case-study research.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the open-data CSV endpoints and WS JERRS web services over scraping the Oracle APEX-style UI; if scraping, respect session/URL parameters (p_lang, p_seznam) and cache entity IDs (IČO) as join keys.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs seed query + ČNB seznamy hub page fetch
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr
CNB list of licensed payment institutions Czech Republic register

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (supervision lists hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Hub page that enumerates every list ČNB publishes (JERRS, WS JERRS, open data, prospectus registers, rating agencies, other lists). Best single entry point for snowballing to all regulator-maintained pointer sources; an EN mirror exists at /en/supervision-financial-market/lists-registers/.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML fetch + link diff to detect newly published lists.
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Otevřená data (open data datasets of regulated entities)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable CSV+JSON-schema exports of ČNB registers published under Government Regulation 425/2016 Sb. Confirmed datasets include banks and foreign bank branches, money changers (směnárny), non-bank consumer credit providers and credit intermediaries, addressed via numbered endpoints (JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N). This is the lowest-friction, highest-fidelity way to maintain a live CZ actor list with IČO keys.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled CSV pull of each p_seznam id, schema-validated against the published *.json schema; enumerate p_seznam ids to discover whether a payment-institution dataset id exists (banks=1, směnárny=2, szsu=3, npsu=7 observed).
queries_used: ČNB otevřená data seznamy JERRS web services XML API poskytovatelé platebních služeb
local_language_terms_used: seznam bank a poboček zahraničních bank

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Webové služby WS JERRS (register web services API)
candidates.why_relevant: Official API over the register, live since 1 July 2019 — the structured, queryable route to entity data (licences, scopes of permitted payment services, changes over time). Important caveat for planning: authentication requires a commercial certificate (eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU trust-list CA), so it is not anonymously accessible.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Assess cost/effort of obtaining a commercial certificate; otherwise fall back to open-data CSV. Read the WSDL/spec on this page before committing.
queries_used: ČNB otevřená data seznamy JERRS web services XML API poskytovatelé platebních služeb
candidates.observed_blocker: Documented requirement for a commercial certificate to authenticate WS JERRS users

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Platební instituce a instituce elektronických peněz (legislative/regulatory base)
candidates.why_relevant: Defines the CZ licence taxonomy (PI, IEP, PPSMR, VEPMR) that any competitor-set model must mirror, and links out to the corresponding registers and rules. Essential for correctly bucketing register entries into payments market segments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off deep read to build the licence-category taxonomy; re-check annually. EN mirror: /en/supervision-financial-market/legislation/payment-and-electronic-money-institutions/.
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Licencování a povolovací řízení: poskytovatelé platebních služeb a vydavatelé elektronických peněz
candidates.why_relevant: Documents how entities enter the register — the licensing pipeline. Useful for anticipating new market entrants and for understanding what documentation (business plan, outsourcing, ICT arrangements) applicants must submit, which indirectly reveals vendor dependencies.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Reference read; monitor for changes in application requirements.
queries_used: CNB list of licensed payment institutions Czech Republic register

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Pravomocná rozhodnutí (final enforcement decisions, proceedings opened after 1.1.2009)
candidates.why_relevant: Full-text sanction and remedial-measure decisions naming specific banks, payment institutions and small-scale providers. These documents frequently describe operational detail — systems, outsourcing arrangements, AML/transaction-monitoring tooling, failures of specific processes — which is otherwise unobtainable vendor/competitor intelligence. Also the earliest public signal of a distressed or exiting competitor.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the listing page for new PDF decisions; extract respondent name/IČO, licence type, date, and any named systems or providers. Parent hub at /cs/dohled-financni-trh/vykon-dohledu/pravomocna-rozhodnuti/ covers other decision classes.
queries_used: ČNB pravomocná rozhodnutí sankce správní řízení platební instituce seznam

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Zprávy o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem (annual supervision reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual reports (archive spanning ~2010 onwards) with counts of licensed entities per category, licensing and sanctioning activity in the payments area, and supervisory priorities. The best single benchmark series for sizing and trending the CZ payments competitor set year over year.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Bulk-download the PDF series (pattern .../zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_YYYY_cz.pdf observed for 2015) and extract entity-count tables. An EN edition is also tabled in Parliament (senat.cz).
queries_used: ČNB zpráva o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem statistika platebního styku
local_language_terms_used: zpráva o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Statistika platebního styku / komentář (payment statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Official harmonised payment statistics: cards issued, POS terminals deployed by CZ acquirers, accounts, transaction counts by payment service and by terminal type. The authoritative denominator for any CZ payments market sizing and the benchmark against which vendor/acquirer share claims are tested (e.g. ~285k POS terminals at end-2025, >16.6m cards mid-2025 per ČNB commentary).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Pull the semi-annual commentary plus the underlying ARAD tables; store as a time series keyed by reporting period.
queries_used: ČNB ARAD databáze časových řad statistika platebního styku karty terminály počet

candidates.source_name: ČNB – ARAD systém časových řad (time series database)
candidates.why_relevant: Public time-series database behind ČNB statistics, with per-report parameterised URLs and export. Gives structured, downloadable history for payments, cards, terminals and banking-sector aggregates instead of PDF snapshots.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the report-id URL pattern (STAT.ARADY_PKG.PARAMETRY_SESTAVY?p_sestuid=...&p_lang=CS) or the newer SPA at /arad/#/cs/home; export CSV per report id.
queries_used: ČNB ARAD databáze časových řad statistika platebního styku karty terminály počet

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků systému CERTIS + Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb
candidates.why_relevant: Versioned lists of direct/indirect participants in the CZ interbank clearing system CERTIS and, separately, of instant-payments participants. This is the operational payments infrastructure map: who clears directly, who piggybacks, and which institutions have gone live on instant payments — a strong proxy for payment-platform vendor projects and partnerships.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the stable 'seznam_certis.pdf' and 'seznam_okamzite_platby.pdf' URLs on a schedule and diff versions; historic versions are retained with a version suffix (e.g. seznam_certis_55.pdf), enabling backfill of participation history.
queries_used: ČNB číselník kódů bank platební systém CERTIS účastníci seznam

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Číselník kódů platebního styku v ČR (ČKPS / bank codes) a Číselníky, seznamy, registry
candidates.why_relevant: The bank-code codelist is the join key between institution names, IBANs and clearing participation, and the hub page also carries the list of payment systems, foreign settlement-system participants, and comparison-website operators under §202 of the Payments Act. Indispensable for entity resolution across all other CZ payments sources.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download kody_bank_CR.pdf (versioned; historic versions carry a numeric suffix) and parse into a code→institution mapping table.
queries_used: ČNB číselník kódů bank platební systém CERTIS účastníci seznam

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Ostatní seznamy (other supervisory lists: payment systems, covered-bond issuers, comparison sites)
candidates.why_relevant: Long tail of niche but high-signal official lists: 'Seznam platebních systémů', foreign settlement/payment-system participants, operators of comparison websites under §202 of the Payments Act, and the list of activities under the limited-network exclusion (which enumerates closed-loop/gift-card style payment schemes normally invisible in registers).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the page's PDF links quarterly; the limited-network activity list is particularly worth diffing for new closed-loop schemes.
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Upozornění pro veřejnost / Upozornění ČNB na aktivity (public warnings, unauthorised providers)
candidates.why_relevant: Names entities operating without ČNB authorisation or misrepresenting ČNB approval. Useful as the negative-space complement to the register: it identifies grey-market payments/investment actors and helps validate that an unfamiliar 'fintech' is not in fact unlicensed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor both this page and the consumer-protection warnings feed at /cs/dohled-financni-trh/ochrana-spotrebitele/upozorneni/.
queries_used: ČNB upozornění varování neoprávněné podnikání finanční trh seznam subjektů

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Stanoviska k regulaci finančního trhu (regulatory opinions, incl. PSD2 / payments scope)
candidates.why_relevant: Numbered supervisory opinions (RSYYYY-NN) interpreting the Payments Act — e.g. 2025 opinions on minimum user experience for payment-initiation services and prohibited obstacles for TPPs, and on whether corporate central payment/collection hubs fall under the Act. These set the supervisory benchmark that shapes what banks and their vendors must build, and flag where enforcement pressure will land next.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the stanoviska index and enumerate RS ids per year; filter for payments/PSD2/digital-finance keywords.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from cs searches on payments regulation
queries_used: ČNB otevřená data seznamy JERRS web services XML API poskytovatelé platebních služeb
ČNB pravomocná rozhodnutí sankce správní řízení platební instituce seznam

candidates.source_name: ČNB – DORA / digitální provozní odolnost finančního trhu (+ SDAT reporting)
candidates.why_relevant: DORA obliges every CZ financial entity to maintain and submit to ČNB a 'registr informací' listing all ICT third-party service providers and contractual arrangements — i.e. a regulator-held, structured map of exactly which vendors serve which Czech banks and payment institutions. The submissions themselves are not public, but ČNB's templates, webinars and reporting guidance define the vendor-relationship data model and are the best available public window onto it.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the DORA page and the SDAT/DORA statistics page for template and taxonomy releases; harvest the webinar decks (PDF) which document the register-of-information fields.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on DORA register of information
queries_used: ČNB DORA registr informací ICT poskytovatelé outsourcing vykazování banky

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Informační povinnosti subjektů finančního trhu / Co nového v dohledu
candidates.why_relevant: Enumerates the reporting obligations each licence category owes ČNB — which tells you what data exists about each competitor, in what granularity and cadence, and therefore what may become publicly derivable. The companion 'Co nového v dohledu' feed is the running change-log of supervisory expectations.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Reference read plus RSS/page-diff monitoring of /cs/dohled-financni-trh/novinky/.
queries_used: ČNB pravomocná rozhodnutí sankce správní řízení platební instituce seznam

candidates.source_name: EBA – Central register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2
candidates.why_relevant: EU-level aggregation of national registers, live since 18 March 2019, downloadable in bulk and free to search. It gives the CZ subset (reported as ~201 entities in one third-party mirror) in a normalised cross-border schema, and crucially captures passporting: which foreign PIs/EMIs/TPPs are notified into CZ and which CZ entities passport out. Complements JERRS rather than replacing it — CZ TPP operation requires both EBA registration and a CZ notification in JERRS.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the register's bulk download, filter home/host country = CZ, and reconcile against ČNB JERRS on IČO/legal name to catch discrepancies and passporting-only actors.
queries_used: EBA register PSD2 payment institutions Czech Republic TPP AISP PISP euclid register

candidates.source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Sbírka rozhodnutí a výroční zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: The statutory ADR body for payment-services and consumer-credit disputes. Its published decisions and annual reports name institutions and describe concrete operational failures — the 2025 annual report flags systemic problems in payment services around misuse of payment instruments in cyber attacks, and a 113% year-on-year rise in disputes. This is close to a public case-study library of CZ payments incidents, and a demand signal for fraud/authentication vendors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the Sbírka rozhodnutí index plus the annual report PDFs; extract institution names, dispute typology and volumes per year.
queries_used: finanční arbitr ČR nálezy rozhodnutí platební styk výroční zpráva

candidates.source_name: ÚOHS – Sbírky rozhodnutí a spojování soutěžitelů (competition authority)
candidates.why_relevant: Merger notifications and competition decisions covering CZ banking/payments — e.g. a ČSOB joint-control notification, an assessment of an ATM-sharing arrangement between several Czech banks, and a decision on the 'vklad na kartu' banking service. Merger and cooperation filings are one of the few sources that document bank–bank and bank–fintech partnerships and market-share reasoning in detail before they are announced commercially. Also published as an open dataset in the national open-data catalogue.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the NKOD open dataset for bulk decision text; separately monitor the 'Oznámení o připravovaném spojení soutěžitelů' feed for early merger signals, filtered on banking/payments NACE and known institution names.
queries_used: ÚOHS sbírka rozhodnutí spojení soutěžitelů banka platební služby

candidates.source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – Platební služby a vypořádání obchodů (legislation, consultations)
candidates.why_relevant: MF ČR, not ČNB, owns the Payments Act (zákon č. 370/2017 Sb.) and runs the public consultations. Consultation dossiers and their published evaluations (e.g. the 2022 PSD2/ZPS evaluation) contain named submissions from banks, fintechs and industry associations — an unusually direct read on which actors exist, what they are building, and who allies with whom. Also the source for the digital-finance act adapting DORA/MiCA (zákon č. 32/2025 Sb.).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the 'aktuality' feed under the payment-services section; harvest consultation evaluation PDFs and extract respondent organisation names as an actor list. Note the domain migration mfcr.cz → mf.gov.cz — track both.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs query on MF ČR payments consultations
queries_used: Ministerstvo financí ČR zákon o platebním styku konzultace fintech digitalizace finančního trhu

candidates.source_name: Financni-subjekty.penize.cz – mirror of ČNB regulated-entity lists
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial re-publication of the ČNB register in a far more scrapable HTML form than JERRS, useful as a fallback or cross-check when JERRS/open-data access is awkward. Secondary source: never authoritative, may lag, and licensing for reuse is unclear — treat ČNB as the system of record.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use only for convenience lookups and cross-validation; check robots.txt and terms before any systematic crawl.
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr
local_language_terms_used: regulované a registrované subjekty finančního trhu

negative_findings.description: No ČNB open-data CSV dataset specifically for payment institutions / e-money institutions / small-scale payment service providers was confirmed on the Otevřená data page. The datasets observed were banks and foreign bank branches (p_seznam=1), money changers (2), credit intermediaries (3, and further categories) and non-bank consumer credit providers (7).
negative_findings.result_summary: Payments-sector entities appear to be reachable via JERRS and possibly WS JERRS, but a dedicated bulk open-data export for platební instituce was not evidenced in the fetched page content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The payments register is the backbone of this cell; if no bulk export exists, collection needs either the certificate-gated WS JERRS API or careful scraping of JERRS, which materially changes the effort estimate.

negative_findings.description: WS JERRS web services require authentication with a commercial certificate from eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU trust-list CA.
negative_findings.result_summary: The official API is not anonymously accessible; this is documented policy rather than a fetch failure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any plan assuming a free public API over the ČNB register is wrong; budget for certificate procurement or design around open data / scraping.

negative_findings.description: The DORA 'registr informací' (register of ICT third-party providers and contractual arrangements) submitted annually by each financial entity to ČNB is a supervisory reporting artefact, not a published register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only ČNB's templates, webinar decks and reporting guidance are public; the actual bank-to-vendor mappings are confidential.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This would be the single most valuable vendor-relationship dataset in the CZ market if it were public. It is not — vendor mapping must be reconstructed from procurement, enforcement decisions, and company disclosures instead.

negative_findings.description: No settled Czech-language term or dedicated regulator page was found for 'case study' / vendor reference project in a supervisory context; searches in cs surfaced only 'stanoviska', 'rozhodnutí' and 'zprávy'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Case-study material from the regulator side exists only implicitly, embedded in enforcement decisions, arbitrator findings and supervision reports.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect a regulator-published case-study source in CZ; case studies must be mined from decision texts or sought in vendor/press cells.

negative_findings.description: No ČNB-published list of pending/ongoing licence applications (a forward-looking pipeline of prospective payment institutions) was found in either cs or en searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the licensing process description and the register of granted authorisations were located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: New-entrant detection will therefore be lagging (visible only on licence grant) unless supplemented by media, funding and trade-register sources.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact JERRS open-data p_seznam id (if any) covering platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, PPSMR and VEPMR was not established; only ids 1, 2, 3 and 7 were evidenced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate p_seznam values against https://jerrs.cnb.cz/apljerrsdad/JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N and record which ids return payments-sector datasets; capture the paired JSON schema for each.

coverage_gaps.description: JERRS search/detail URL patterns were not mapped — only the login/entry URL was observed. Deep-link structure for a single entity record and for a filtered list by licence type is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Interactively walk JERRS in a browser, capture the URL/parameter grammar for entity detail pages and licence-type filters, and record whether stable permalinks by IČO exist.

coverage_gaps.description: AML supervision (Finanční analytický úřad, FAÚ) and cyber/ICT supervision (NÚKIB) were not searched in this slice; both regulate CZ payment providers and publish annual reports and, in FAÚ's case, guidance naming typologies and obliged-entity categories.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run cs queries such as 'Finanční analytický úřad výroční zpráva povinné osoby platební instituce' and 'NÚKIB regulovaný subjekt bankovnictví významný informační systém' and add resulting sources.

coverage_gaps.description: The relationship between the ČNB JERRS entry set and the EBA PSD2 register CZ subset (reported as ~201 entities via a third-party mirror, not verified at EBA) has not been reconciled, including passporting-in TPPs that have no CZ establishment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the EBA register bulk file, filter home/host = CZ, and diff against JERRS on legal name and national identifier to produce a single deduplicated CZ payments actor master list.

coverage_gaps.description: Register snapshots are point-in-time; no evidence was found of a ČNB-published historical archive of register states, so entry/exit history of payment institutions cannot be reconstructed from the register alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Begin snapshotting the registers and CERTIS/instant-payments participant PDFs on a fixed cadence to build an internal time series; backfill partially from versioned CERTIS PDFs and annual supervision reports.

brief: The CZ regulator layer is unusually rich and almost entirely public: ČNB's JERRS application is the legally mandated, canonical enumeration of every bank, payment institution, e-money institution, small-scale payment provider and notified PSD2 TPP, with partial machine-readable exports via the Otevřená data CSV endpoints and a certificate-gated WS JERRS API. Around that core sit high-value pointer and benchmark sources: CERTIS and instant-payments participant lists (the real payments infrastructure map), the ČKPS bank-code codelist for entity resolution, harmonised payment statistics and ARAD time series for market sizing, and the pravomocná rozhodnutí enforcement archive plus annual supervision reports for operational and vendor detail found nowhere else. Beyond ČNB, the Financial Arbitrator's decision collection, ÚOHS merger and cooperation decisions, and MF ČR consultation dossiers each expose partnerships, incidents and actor names that registers alone omit; the EBA PSD2 register adds the passporting dimension. The main constraints are access mechanics rather than availability — the payments-specific bulk export id is unconfirmed, JERRS deep-link structure is unmapped, the API needs a commercial certificate, and the DORA register of ICT providers (the ideal vendor map) is supervisory-confidential.
